title: PairCoder Real-Paper Regression
paperText:
# Abstract
PairCoder adapts pair programming to LLM-based code generation through a Navigator for high-level planning and a Driver for implementation. It achieves relative pass@1 improvements of 12.00%-162.43% compared with direct prompting.
# Problem
Existing code-generation approaches rely on a rigid single solution plan. When the initial plan is flawed, feedback-driven repair remains trapped in the wrong direction.
# Method
The Navigator reflects on the problem, samples and clusters diverse plans, selects a current plan, and switches plans using execution feedback and historical memory. The Driver generates, tests, and repairs code. Algorithm 1 repeats until public tests pass or the iteration limit is reached. Figure 2 shows the complete Navigator-Driver workflow.
# Experiments
The evaluation uses HumanEval, HumanEval+, MBPP, MBPP+, and CodeContest with GPT-3.5-Turbo and DeepSeek-Coder. Table 2 reports the primary pass@1 comparison.
# Results
PairCoder outperforms all baselines. Relative gains are 16.97%-162.43% with GPT-3.5-Turbo and 12.00%-128.76% with DeepSeek-Coder. Figure 9 shows that accuracy continues to improve with more iterations. Ablation results show that both multi-plan exploration and feedback-driven refinement contribute, with larger gains on CodeContest.
# Limitations
PairCoder requires more API calls than most approaches, although token consumption remains moderate. Results may also be affected by benchmark leakage and public-test coverage.
# Contributions
The paper is the first to adapt pair programming to LLM code generation, introduces multi-plan exploration and feedback-driven refinement, and validates the framework on five benchmarks.
Figure 2 presents PairCoder. Figure 9 presents iteration curves. Table 2 presents the primary comparison.
